questions.question: How is water and oil removed from an air storage tank?

options.text: The water and oil are siphoned out.
A drain valve is opened to let the water and oil out.
The water and oil are removed automatically when the brakes are used.
A sponge is used to soak up the water and oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve is opened to let the water and oil out.
questions.explanation: Water and oil are removed from air storage tanks using a drain valve. If left in the tank, water and oil can damage the brakes. Manually operated tanks must be drained every day.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should be:

options.text: Done the same way every time.
Not required to check all items every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Done the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you do not skip anything.

questions.question: After picking up passengers, you should:

options.text: Wait for passengers to sit down or hold on before driving.
Honk your horn and pull into traffic right away.
Start driving as fast as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for passengers to sit down or hold on before driving.
questions.explanation: Start and stop smoothly to prevent passenger injury. After passengers board, give them time to sit or hold on before you start driving.

questions.question: A disruptive passenger should be:

options.text: Removed from the bus right away, no matter where you are.
Let off at the next bus stop.
Kept on the bus and taken to the police station.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let off at the next bus stop.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for a passenger's safety, even if they are disruptive. Let them off at the next scheduled stop or in a safe, well-lit area with other people around.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay far away from them.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of room and keep a safe distance behind them.

questions.question: When checking wiper blades, they should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tight and firm.
questions.explanation: Check your wiper blades for damage and to make sure they are secure. The rubber should not be stiff or damaged.

questions.question: In a basic vehicle control skills test, you must be able to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Alley dock.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes straight line backing, offset backing, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should be no more than:
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 degrees.
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This is about two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel. Too much play makes it hard to steer.

questions.question: You should watch for black ice:

options.text: When it is below freezing and the road looks wet.
When it is above freezing and there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is below freezing and the road looks wet.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. Watch for black ice when the temperature is below freezing and the road surface looks wet.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, you should:

options.text: Pull the brake pedal toward you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press down the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To stop an air-braked vehicle, press the brake pedal down. Control the pressure so the vehicle stops smoothly and safely.

questions.question: Looking far ahead when driving is:

options.text: Not helpful because your current location is more important.
A good practice to spot hazards early.
Only needed when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good practice to spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: When driving, look 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This helps you notice hazards early and gives you time to react safely.

questions.question: Good drivers look ____ seconds ahead of their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This distance lets you react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: When a bus stops at a stop or final destination, passengers should be told:
questions.correctAnswerText: The location.
questions.explanation: The driver should announce the stop location, why you are stopping, when the bus will leave next, and the bus number.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of driver fatigue?
questions.correctAnswerText: Staying in your lane
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, not remembering recent miles, missing exits, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: Headlights:

options.text: Are usually not needed at night.
Produce better light than the sun.
Should be on high beam when it is safe and legal.
Should always be on high beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be on high beam when it is safe and legal.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights at night when safe and legal. Switch to low beam when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle to avoid blinding other drivers.

questions.question: To prevent a vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly engage the clutch.
questions.explanation: For vehicles with manual transmission, slightly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal. This prevents the vehicle from rolling backward.

questions.question: Why should part of your vehicle be visible in a properly adjusted side mirror?

options.text: It limits the view behind the trailer.
It gives you a reference point for judging distance.
It lets you see stickers on the side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a reference point for judging distance.
questions.explanation: A properly adjusted side mirror should show part of your vehicle. This gives you a reference point to judge where nearby objects are located.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts because:

options.text: Rain mixes with oil on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first falls, it mixes with oil and grease on the road, creating a slippery film. As rain continues, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, oil pressure should:

options.text: Build up slowly over a few minutes.
Reach normal levels within a few seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reach normal levels within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal levels within seconds of starting the engine.

questions.question: Shaded areas of a road:

options.text: Stay icy after ice melts in sunny areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay icy after ice melts in sunny areas.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and warm up slower. They remain icy and slippery after ice has melted in other areas of the road.
